answer: Neighborhood curvature weighting. Each identity's weight is set by the local clustering of its transaction graph: edges whose endpoints share few mutual neighbors carry little flow. A ripple of value across a sparse, star-shaped cluster attenuates, so newly minted identities must first build dense, overlapping links to real peers. Reaching the juniper threshold—enough shared neighbors to route meaningful volume—requires many real counterparties per identity.
